ai_summary.headline: Cash is about 23% of a heavily underfunded plan, but almost all of it is sectoral; MPC is under 1%.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP plans CVA of just under $400M for more than 10 million people, but MPC is only $15M for 688,300 people, under 4% of CVA [s1]. FSAC ($262M) and ES/NFI ($111M) dominate [s1]. The plan seeks $1.71bn for 17.5M targeted [s2]. FTS shows $559.7M received by late October 2026, about 33% [s3]. MPC has received $19.2M against its $14.7M requirement, 131% on FTS's single-cluster view ($26.9M on the shared-cluster view) [s3]; this likely reflects funding tagged to MPC beyond the planned line, so the small MPC plan line may understate donor appetite. 65% of people prefer cash or a cash/in-kind mix [s1]. The standard transfer is $170 per household, with a 20% top-up for female-headed and disability households [s1]. Weekly WFP market reports continue [s4]. Gaps are large: no MSNA modality split, no cost-efficiency comparison, no feasibility study, and no confirmed current CWG leads. Inference: MPC could be scaled within existing funding, and CALP messaging might focus on that.
barriers: MPC is a very small share of CVA, so flexibility for households is limited
Plan about one-third funded by late October 2026, forcing prioritisation
Assistance is compressed to 1-3 months at $170 per household
No named social protection system to link cash to
opportunities: Differentiated transfer values (+20%) are a replicable design feature
Functioning weekly market reporting and active financial service providers
data_gaps: cost-efficiency for MPC, vouchers and in-kind
